newsitem.title: USA: Consumer incomes up strongly in June, spending rises.
newsitem.headline: Consumer incomes up strongly in June, spending rises.

text.p: Consumers' incomes rose strongly and their spending increased steadily in June as job opportunities expanded, the Commerce Department said on Friday.
Incomes from wages, salaries and all other sources grew by 0.6 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of $6.87 trillion while spending rose 0.3 percent to $5.45 trillion.
The strong rise in incomes suggests consumers have the buying power to keep the expansion on track, since spending fuels about two-thirds of national economic activity.
Wall Street economists had forecast that June incomes would rise by a smaller 0.4 percent and that spending would increase 0.4 percent from May.
The June income rise was twice the 0.3 percent gain posted in May while the spending increase matched May's 0.3 percent pickup.

Consumers socked more away into bank accounts and other savings vehicles during June. Savings rose to 4.4 cents out of each dollar earned from 4.1 cents in May as savings increased to a rate of $258.5 billion from $241.8 billion in May.
A steadily expanding economy has provided abundant job opportunities and bolstered consumer confidence and willingness to spend.

Gains in personal income, which includes wages and salaries as well as income from sources such as dividends, interest and businesses, are essential for funding consumer purchases that fuel two-thirds of national economic activity.

The department said private-sector wages and salaries increased by $31.8 billion in June, compared with a smaller rise of $12 billion in May. Employment, hourly earnings and the average workweek all grew in June, the department noted.
The Labour Department reported on Friday that another 316,000 jobs were created in July and that the national unemployment rate dropped to 4.8 percent of the workforce.
Spending on durable goods, which includes cars, fell slightly in June by 0.6 percent to an annual rate of $642.7 billion in June from $646.4 billion in May.
But spending on nondurable products climbed 0.3 percent to a rate of $1.582 trillion from $1.578 trillion in May while spending for services was up to $3.22 trillion from $3.206 trillion in May.
Payrolls of manufacturing companies rose to an annual rate of $702.3 billion in June from $700.4 billion in May.
